reason: The cited evidence supports that high entropy stabilizes a single phase and improves corrosion resistance (E2), and that HEA catalysts show enhanced stability/durability (E3, E5). However, none of the cited passages directly demonstrate reduced PGM consumption, and the evidence for improved catalytic activity is from different material systems (spinel oxides, E1) or specific doped systems (E4) rather than a general HEA replacement for automotive exhaust catalysts. The key premise of PGM reduction is unsupported.
premises: High configurational entropy in HEAs suppresses phase separation and secondary phase formation, yielding a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
This homogeneous single-phase structure enhances structural integrity and resistance to corrosion/dissolution under harsh conditions.
HEA catalysts exhibit improved long-term stability and durability compared to conventional catalysts.
HEA catalysts can provide enhanced catalytic activity relative to conventional catalysts.
The use of HEAs can reduce platinum-group-metal consumption.
